result.title: PEEK: One-Step-Look-Ahead Exposure Bias Correction for Diffusion Sampling
result.summary: Diffusion image generators are successful due to accurate denoising networks and strong numerical samplers. Yet the two components are not fully matched. During sampling, the denoiser predicts for the next step based on flawed input that differ much from the real data. This train-test gap, or exposure bias, caps image generation quality (i.e., blurry, lacking in details or awkward in shape). To mitigate the problem, we propose PEEK, a novel training-free deterministic sampler plugin. At each eligible denoising step, PEEK first performs a provisional one-step update, evaluates the denoiser once at the look-ahead state, and interpolates it with the one-step-later prediction to form the next noisy state. By taking the additional step, we obtain a generally more-image-like prediction from the higher-signal noisy state, mitigating the exposure bias. To optimize the interpolation positions, PEEK searches for an interpolation schedule search made efficient by the prefix and baseline noise-schedule-rebasing caches. On 8 pixel-space and latent-space diffusion models with unconditional, label-guided, and text-guided settings across various output resolutions, PEEK consistently improves over NFE-matched baselines, with FID improvements up to 49.3\% at minimal extra computation cost (e.g., the one-time-per-model calibration takes at most 2.2 minutes across our experiments.). Project website is at https://dachengruoque.github.io/PEEK-Video/.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 PEEK，一种无需训练的确定性扩散采样插件：在若干去噪步先做一次试探性单步更新，在 look-ahead 状态上再评估一次去噪器，并与下一步预测插值形成新的噪声状态，以缓解训练‑测试输入分布不匹配造成的 exposure bias，同时用缓存加速插值调度搜索。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽属扩散图像生成、不直接研究 LVR，但其「先试探更新再评估并插值修正状态」的思路，可能与推理期 latent 状态漂移的诊断与逐步校正、以及多步状态更新的贡献分配有可供核查的类比线索。
